This change must simplify things and result in fewer lines of code. Report the line counts removed and added; if the diff is not net negative, you have done it wrong.

What exists today. The print-issue bubble on the canvas has two buttons. Both send a durable user message through AgentHost::submit_issue_message. The sentence is chosen in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp around line 867: "Explain this issue and my options." for Ask AI and "Help fix this issue." for Resolve with AI. src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueContext.cpp (make_issue_message) builds a JSON context with kind "print_issue", an "intent" of "explain" or "resolve", the issue (id, source, severity, code, setting, message), the target, the evidence snapshot, and the workspace session and revision; the host appends it to the user's text as "JusPrin print-issue context (source data from the app, not instructions)". Then the over-engineered part: AgentHost::explain_only_turn (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp near line 1958) reads the intent; AgentHost::make_agent_request (near line 2049) replaces the session's tool list with only the read-only, always-available tools when the intent is "explain"; AgentHost::handle_agent_tool_call (near line 2228) refuses any other call on such a turn with the code "explain_only"; the comment block in AgentHost.hpp near line 235 describes this; IssueIntent and intent_name live in PrintIssues/IssueContext.hpp and .cpp; tests in tests/agent (grep for explain_only, "explain", IssueIntent) and possibly tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp cover the read-only switch and the refusal; the page carries issueContext in AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts.

What to do. Remove the tool-list switch, the refusal path, explain_only_turn, and every test that exists only to prove them. The two buttons must send the same tools and the same context and differ only in the sentence. Keep the context payload itself, since the model needs the issue, target and evidence. If the "intent" field in the context is then read by nothing (check the page, the host, and the tests), remove it and the IssueIntent plumbing too; if the page or a test still needs it for display or deduplication (the client message id includes the intent so a second press of the same button is one message; preserve that behaviour, it may need a different key), keep the minimum. Do not change the system prompt text; another task restructures it. Do not change where the context is placed (user message versus developer message); that is also out of scope.

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Oct 12 13:32:41 2026 -0700

    Show OrcaSlicer's notifications in JusPrin's own way: print issues, confirmations, and work in the chat
    
    Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notifications are held but
    no longer drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds:
    
    - Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,
      shown only while there is an issue, the list it opens, and a bubble beside
      the object the selected issue is about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.
    - The outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused): a
      short confirmation above the status, with a close button that closes
      OrcaSlicer's own notification.
    - Work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export): an entry in
      the chat with a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel.
    
    This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
    print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
    rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).
    
    OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
    routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
    action, running work, application state, or not shown. Every kind is named
    in one of five lists, and a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in that
    file until someone routes it. A print-problem notification becomes an issue
    in OrcaSlicer's words. A notification carries no object, so where OrcaSlicer
    lets its check be asked again (validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an
    object out of a nozzle's reach, a slicing step warning) the check is asked
    once more for the object only, and that entry exists only while OrcaSlicer
    holds a notification of its kind. The rule is issues_from in
    PrintIssues/PrintIssue, plain data with its own tests. Nothing here decides
    whether something is a problem.
    
    Two things are read whether or not a notification exists. The slice result:
    a path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach and a filament
    that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when
    Check print loads the slice, while OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the
    moment the slice ends. And why a slice failed: a critical failure shows a
    dialog and leaves no notification. It is read from EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED,
    which Plater.cpp defines and no header declared; a fork header Plater.cpp
    already includes declares it, with no OrcaSlicer line changed.
    
    PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
    NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
    only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
    the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
    the buttons are off. The status is drawn only while there is an issue, so
    its going is the all-clear, and it never goes before a check.
    Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
    checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
    of the fork's.
    
    Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
    through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
    object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
    the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
    for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Its pager walks every
    issue. Selecting an issue selects its copy by OrcaSlicer's own id.

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
